lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Carhenge — the proposed redevelopment at 700 W. Pacific Avenue hits two separate hearings on September 30: a special HARC session reviewing preliminary architecture for all building clusters, and a Town Council appeal hearing on the lot subdivision that a law firm challenged just two weeks after P&Z approved it. Alongside that, the Gondola Leadership Committee takes up a genuinely consequential choice between federal funding and local project control, and the County Commissioners dig into a proposed Employee Housing Impact Fee in a work session Tuesday.

notable.stake: Council decides: federal dollars with strings or local financing for the gondola.
HARC reviews three preliminary large-scale applications for the Carhenge redevelopment.
Town Council hears appeal that could block the Carhenge lot consolidation entirely.
County could advance a new Employee Housing Impact Fee affecting future development.
Final architecture review for 15 employee apartments and 4 new multifamily units.
